Compounded sales growth stands at -3% over 10 years, -2% over 5 years, -8% over 3 years, and -5% over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14, E15, E16], directly confirming a poor five-year sales growth trend of -2.23% [E55] while the broader sector achieves a median sales growth of 12.5% [E68]. This top-line contraction is compounded by severe unprofitability, evidenced by a negative P/E ratio of -31.54x against a sector benchmark of 17.73x [E5], alongside deeply negative returns on assets at -10.12% and equity at -5.9% compared to respective sector benchmarks of 4.63% and 8.42% [E7, E8]. Investors receive zero compensation for taking on these operational losses, as the dividend yield is a barren 0.00% [E3]. Furthermore, the market demands an exorbitant price-to-book multiple of 4.06x on a book value of ₹ 6.65 [E1]—representing a P/B of 4.03x against a sector benchmark of just 1.79x [E6]—which severely overprices a shrinking and structurally unprofitable business. Conceded: [E13, E14, E15, E16, E55, E1, E6, E3, E5, E7, E8]. Furthermore, this positive top-line momentum is directly paired with accelerating earnings growth [E60], signaling a profound operational turnaround that historical multi-year averages fail to reflect. Trading at 66% of its 52-week range [E4], the market capitalisation of ₹ 1,322 Cr [E2] provides an attractive entry ahead of this newly awakened growth profile.

Conceded: [E58, E60]. While the bull points to these recent screen reasons of year-over-year sales expansion and accelerating earnings growth, they do not erase a persistent, multi-year history of top-line destruction spanning ten years (-3%) [E13], five years (-2%) [E14], three years (-8%) [E15], and the trailing twelve months (-5%) [E16], culminating in an official flag for poor five-year sales growth [-2.23%] [E55] that severely lags the sector median sales growth of 12.5% [E68]. Furthermore, celebrating this minor recent uptick ignores the company's catastrophic fundamental profitability metrics, including a deeply negative P/E of -31.54x against a sector benchmark of 17.73x [E5], a disastrous ROA of -10.12% compared to the sector's 4.63% [E7], and an abysmal ROE of -5.9% versus a sector benchmark of 8.42% [E8]. Investors paying a rich price-to-book ratio of 4.06x [E1] (or 4.03x against a sector benchmark of 1.79x) [E6] for a ₹ 1,322 Cr market capitalization [E2] receive a 0.00% dividend yield [E3] while backing a chronically shrinking business whose stock sits elevated at 66% of its 52-week range [E4] on the back of fleeting signals rather than durable operational success.
